solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wizard banner returned and brought in

indicators.note: brought in means the next word is placed inside the reversed letters
returned means the word for banner is read backwards

parts.note: a banner is a flag
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes a flag that was sent back and then carried indoors by a magician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banner' reads as a headline or flag in the surface; here it is just a flag, turned round before the joining word goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Gandalf is the famous wizard in Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings.

clue.text: Become somewhat fidgety

indicators.note: somewhat says only a part of the following word is wanted, here its middle letters

explanation.surface: An instruction or observation that someone is growing a little restless.
explanation.definitionFit: To get, as in 'get angry', is a common synonym for to become.

clue.text: Close match that's not put on till late?

definitions.text: that's not put on till late?

parts.note: close means near, which is nigh
a match or contest that ends level is a tie

explanation.surface: A tight sporting contest that is not scheduled until late in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the garment is only put on at bedtime, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, worn only when going to bed late in the day.

clue.text: Tree is more bare, having top removed

indicators.note: having top removed means the first letter of the word is cut off, top because this is a down clue

parts.note: balder means more bare, having less hair

explanation.surface: A tree is described as barer than before, its crown lopped off.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a deciduous tree of the birch family growing near water.

clue.text: Dissenting group force lawsuit

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
a lawsuit is a legal action

explanation.surface: A breakaway group is pressing ahead with litigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a small dissident party within a larger organisation.

clue.text: Mark one in staff that represents authority

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone is told to label one item among the official staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a ceremonial staff carried as a symbol of office, as in Parliament.

clue.text: Painting artist stuffed into Scottish chimney turned up

indicators.note: stuffed into means the artist goes inside the reversed letters
turned up means the word is read upwards, so backwards in this down clue

parts.note: lum is the Scots word for a chimney
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter has been crammed up a chimney in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reverses the word, since it is read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A mural is a painting done directly on a wall.

clue.text: In university, arrived to speak on card game

indicators.note: on means the first part sits above the second in this down clue
to speak means the word for arrived is taken by its sound

parts.note: came means arrived, which said aloud gives CAM, the river
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone got to a university and then talked about a game of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambridge is one of England's two ancient universities, standing on the River Cam.

clue.text: Way too old maybe to be presented in theatre

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
aged means old, and 'too old maybe' is an example sense

explanation.surface: A play may be too dated to be put on in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that is staged has been produced and performed on stage.

clue.text: Check more unusual protective coating

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of the next word are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to inspect a coating that is more out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium plating, a shiny layer applied to resist corrosion.

clue.text: Provide food and support — grub

parts.note: to cater is to provide food
a pillar is a supporting column

explanation.surface: A caterer's slogan: supply meals and backing, then the word 'grub' for food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like food in the surface; here it is the larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar is the larva of a butterfly or moth, and grub is another word for an insect larva.

clue.text: In street unending party getting louder and louder

indicators.note: unending means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a crescent is a curved street
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A street party that never stops gets ever noisier.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a musical passage of gradually increasing loudness.

clue.text: Happened to fit iron in ring

indicators.note: fit means to install the iron inside the ring word
in confirms the iron goes inside the ring word

parts.note: to ring is to sound a bell, and a bell is a ring
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Something occurred so that iron was fitted into a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Befell is the past tense of befall, meaning to happen to someone.

clue.text: Spooner's crazy convicts have mildly pornographic publications?

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words

parts.note: mad means crazy
lags is British slang for convicts

explanation.surface: Deranged prisoners are found with saucy magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the M of MAD and the L of LAGS to get LAD MAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lad mags are British men's magazines such as Loaded and Nuts, known for racy photo shoots.

clue.text: Not one criticism of thin wine?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: no person at all
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words, NO BODY, which is what a wine critic says of a thin wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobody means no person, and a wine without fullness of flavour is said to lack body.

clue.text: Gusto shown over half of cheese roll

indicators.note: over means the first part sits above the second in this down clue

parts.note: brio means vigour or gusto

indicators.note: half of means only the first three of the word's six letters are kept

explanation.surface: Enthusiasm is displayed over part of a cheese roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a sweet, light French bread roll.

clue.text: African country that may produce erotic video

indicators.note: may produce means the letters can be rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion that some nation might be the source of a sex film.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is French for Ivory Coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cote d'Ivoire is the official name of the Ivory Coast in West Africa.

clue.text: Fierce type good in row

indicators.note: in means the letter for good is placed inside the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: An aggressive person behaving well during an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' may suggest a quarrel; here it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is a fierce big cat, and the word is used for any fierce, aggressive person.

clue.text: Worth siting university in dale

indicators.note: siting means placing the university letter at a location within the dale word
in shows the university letter goes inside the dale word

parts.note: a vale is a valley, like a dale

explanation.surface: An estimate of the merit of building a university in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Value means worth, the importance or price of something.

clue.text: Riddle that had many variations

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a puzzle or mystery
second meaning: the theme of Elgar's ... Variations

explanation.walkthrough: Elgar's Enigma Variations is a set of fourteen orchestral variations on an original theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzling mystery, and Elgar named his famous Variations after one.

clue.text: Voracious eater's place at head of table

parts.note: locus is Latin for place, used in English for a location

indicators.note: at head of means only the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A greedy diner sits at the top of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Locusts swarm and devour crops, so the insect is a byword for a voracious feeder.

clue.text: Star has gone down? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: sunk means has gone down, as a ship

explanation.surface: A star asks whether it has set, and is told almost.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system.

clue.text: Boundary is square

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket a ball hit to the boundary along the ground scores a ...
second meaning: a square number, two times two

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a boundary is a hit reaching the edge of the field, scoring four runs (or six if it clears the rope).
explanation.definitionFit: Four is both a cricket boundary hit and the perfect square of two.

clue.text: Female, busy type, finally down in drinking den

parts.note: she is a female person
a bee is proverbially busy

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A busy woman ends up drinking in a dive bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed bar, especially in Ireland or South Africa.
